newsitem.title: USA: Toshiba to sell desktop PCs in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to sell desktop PCs in U.S.

text.p: Toshiba Corp., a leading maker of laptop computers, said Tuesday it will introduce desktop computers to the U.S. home computer market.
The new line, called the Infinia, will sell from $1,699 to $2,799 and will be aimed primarily at the consumer market.
Industry executives are predicting that home computers will eventually become the centre of a home network, controlling many different appliances from one machine.
The new desktop takes a step in that direction.
Toshiba designed the Infinia like many consumer appliances, with a sleek black housing for the moniter, hard drive, keyboard and mouse.

The machines will also have the features of several home appliances in one unit. Toshiba's InTouch Modules and InTouch Remote will give one-touch access for checking telephone messages, making phone calls, playing a compact disc or tuning into television or FM radio.
Like many appliances, comsumers will be able to adjust volume with a simple dial on the InTouch module, rather than changing settings in the computer's programmes.
Toshiba said it plans to expand its desktop market by selling the computers to corporate users in the first quarter of 1997, and will add servers for business networks by early 1998.
The Infinia line uses Intel Corp.'s Pentium 133MHz, Pentium 166MHz and Pentium 200MHz chips and has hard drives ranging up to three gigabytes.

The line has 16 megabyte or 32MB standard memory, expandable to 128MB, as well as a 28.8 kilobits per second modem, with software upgradable to 33.6 kbps and Digital Simultaneous Voice Data capabilities.
